newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian shares close down, more losses expected.
newsitem.headline: Austrian shares close down, more losses expected.

text.p: Austrian shares ended lower on Wednesday, mirroring international markets, and traders predicted further downside was likely.
"There is so much nervousness in the market at the moment, politicians are coming out with a lot of negative comments," said one trader.
Dealers said the index could well slide to 1100 points. Strong resistance is seen around 1145.
The ATX index tumbled 6.09 points or 0.54 percent to 1121.88. Four ATX shares rose, 15 fell, two remained unchanged.
Buying interest was selective amidst volatile trade, according to traders.
Insurer EA Generali was the top loser, dropping 4.49 percent to 3400.0 schillings.
"That was certainly linked with the (rumoured) Bank Austria offer for Creditanstalt," said one trader.

Creditanstalt preferred shares climbed six schillings to 520.0 on rumours of a possible bid for the government's stake in the flagship bank by Bank Austria. Creditanstalt ordinary shares closed unchanged at 719.50 schillings. Bids must be in by December 16.

Bank Austria is rumoured to be on the brink of putting in a 16 billion schilling offer for Creditanstalt. The only known bidder for the bank so far is an Italo-Austro-German consortium around EA Generali, which has offered 10 billion schillings for two thirds of the government's stake.
"There's a lot of speculation in the market that it (a Bank Austria bid) will drive up the bid of the consortium," another trader noted.
Shares in Bank Austria were suspended on bourses in Vienna, Brussels and Frankfurt.
The leading gainer of the session was brick maker Wienerberger, gaining 1.65 percent to 2,100 schillings.
The December ATX future dropped 15 points to 115.0.
The broad-based Vienna Bourse index shed 2.30 points or 0.54 percent to 424.88. -- Vienna newsroom, +431 53112257
